title: A failed migration surfaces a specific error code and leaves the on-disk store unchanged
description: When a migration statement or its version bookkeeping row fails, the migration runner rolls back the transaction, throws an error with a stable code and a message naming the failing version and the description of that migration, and does not attempt further migrations. The on-disk schema version reflects the last successfully committed migration, not the failed one. The store facade propagates the failure to the caller of the open entry point.
rationale: Silent partial migrations are the shape that produces the worst production incidents: the store is in a state no code knows how to interpret and the operator has no error to search on. A stable error code that names the failing version turns the diagnostic loop into a one-step operation (open the migration, read the statement, fix, redeploy).
